## Trainer

Choose a **style**, a **level** and where the **bass** plays, then press **Start**. You hear the melody with a bass line under it
(no chords), then a bass line alone. Was it the same line? **Space** plays both again, **S** / **D** answer, **Enter** goes on.
Your settings and your last ten answers at each level stay in this browser.

<div id="bass-ear"></div>

## The levels

| Level | Where the bass plays | What may differ |
|---|---|---|
| 1 · Chord roots | chord changes, always (the style and **Bass on** are ignored) | one chord on another root of the key |
| 2 · Roots: a different chord | chord changes | one chord's root, a third away (I for vi, IV for ii, V for iii) |
| 3 · Roots: inversions | chord changes | the 3rd or 5th of a chord in the bass instead of the root, or a different root |
| 4 · Macrobeats: chord tones | each macrobeat | one note goes to another note of the same chord |
| 5 · An embellishment in or out | each macrobeat | one embellishment added or taken away |
| 6 · Which embellishment? | every beat | one embellishment swapped for another |
| 7 · Walking: a step apart | every beat | one note a scale step away |
| 8 · Walking: a semitone apart | every beat | one note a semitone away (a chromatic approach from above instead of below) |
| 9 · Anything | left to chance | any of these, any tune |

Half the questions are "same". **♫ Show notation** (any time; it stays on until you turn it off) shows the first line with
the melody and chord symbols on a grand staff. The second line appears after you answer, with the changed notes marked ▼; before
you answer, a button shows it early. The bass is written an octave above where it sounds, as bass parts are. After you answer you see what changed and where, the tune and its chords, and you can hear each bass
line alone. Levels 1–3 use the easiest tunes, 7–8 the harder ones; **Tune** can pick any tune or one tune.

## Where the bass plays

**Bass on** overrides the level:

- **Only on chord changes**: one note a chord, held. Best for hearing reharmonisations and inversions.
- **Each downbeat and change**: a note at the start of every bar as well.
- **Each macrobeat**: in 2/4 every quarter, in 4/4 and 2/2 every half, in 3/4 every bar (dotted half), in 6/8 every dotted quarter.
  This is Gordon's macrobeat in usual duple and triple meter (*Learning Sequences in Music*, pp. 175–176).
- **Every beat**: every quarter (every dotted quarter in 6/8). In the jazz style this walks.
- **Leave it to chance**: the changes, and about half of the other beats.

With fewer notes the embellishment levels have less to work with, so a question may fall back to an inversion or a different root.

## The styles

Each style has its own embellishments. The lines are made fresh each time from the tune's chord symbols, in the style's idiom: they are
this site's inventions, not transcriptions. *Unverified:* the descriptions of each idiom below are from memory and not yet checked
against a source.

| Style | Embellishments it uses |
|---|---|
| **MLT (Gordon)** | roots and fifths on the macrobeats, an octave, a passing tone now and then |
| **Rock and pop** | roots, eighth-note pumping, octaves, a fifth, a scale step into the next chord |
| **Jazz** | two-feel roots and fifths, chord tones, walking steps, a chromatic approach on the last beat before a change |
| **Classical** | passing and neighbour tones, the bass by step, first inversions to smooth the line |

## The tunes

135 tunes from the [Tune Library](tunes.qmd), the first eight bars of each, chosen by `scripts/bass-ear-corpus.mjs` from the
786 with chord symbols that it can read. A tune is left out when it has only one chord, unreadable chord symbols, chords that begin
late, or a meter other than 2/4, 3/4, 4/4, 2/2 or 6/8. Each is put in a tier:

- **Tier 1**: two or three chords, all in the key, at most one change a bar (Lightly Row, Bell Horses, Lucy Locket).
- **Tier 2**: more chords or faster changes, at most one outside the key (many standards).
- **Tier 3**: chords outside the key, slash chords, extended jazz harmony.

Within a tier, tunes with a change every bar or so, a melody that is not too busy and a melody well above the bass come first.

## For teachers

- Same is easier to hear than different (*Learning Sequences in Music*, p. 219). Start at level 1 (chord roots only), then
  move to macrobeats before the walking levels.
- Melody on the band's piano (or a guitar), bass on the band's bass. No chords, no drums. **Second time** can play the melody again
  with the second line, which is harder: the melody has to be heard past.
- Not yet: the tune's own written bass lines (none of the tunes in the library has a bass part), and
  saving results to a class account.
